'''Ariel Washington Hukporti''' (born 12 April 2002) is a German professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA).

==Early life and youth career==
Hukporti was born in [[Stralsund]], northern Germany to [[Togo]]lese parents and was raised by a single mother.<ref name="klumpp">{{cite web |last1=Klumpp |first1=Joachim |title=Ariel Hukporti – das Basketball-Talent hat nur ein Ziel: die NBA |url=https://www.stuttgarter-nachrichten.de/inhalt.mhp-riesen-ludwigsburg-ariel-hukporti-das-basketball-talent-hat-nur-ein-ziel-die-nba.d68331e1-47b3-4148-8628-e4cd0157fdf9.html |website=[[Stuttgarter Nachrichten]] |accessdate=2 April 2020 |language=German |date=11 March 2020}}</ref> He grew up playing [[association football|football]] as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]]. Hukporti stood {{height|m=1.80}} at age nine and started playing basketball when he was 11 years old, in part due to his height.<ref name=klumpp/><ref name="big">{{cite web |title=BIG-Appetizer: Ariel Hukporti |url=https://www.big-basketball.de/index.php/news/big-appetizer/717-appetizer-ariel-hukporti |publisher=BIG Basketball |accessdate=2 April 2020 |language=German |date=16 June 2018}}</ref> He began playing in the Jugend Basketball Bundesliga, the German U16 league, with USC Freiburg. After one season, he received offers from renowned clubs, including [[FC Bayern Munich (basketball)|Bayern Munich]] and [[Brose Bamberg]]. He decided to continue his career with [[Riesen Ludwigsburg]] and its junior team, Porsche BBA Ludwigsburg.<ref name=big/><ref name="hein">{{cite web |last1=Hein |first1=David |title=Hukporti still plenty raw, Crailsheim with two possible gems |url=http://www.heinnews.com/basketball/international-basketball/fiba-basketball/hukporti-still-plenty-raw-crailsheim-with-two-possible-gems/ |publisher=Heinnews |accessdate=2 April 2020 |date=23 January 2017}}</ref>

In December 2018, at the [[2018–19 Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament|Adidas Next Generation Tournament]] (ANGT) [[2018–19 Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament#Valencia|Valencia]], Hukporti averaged 18 points, 15.2 rebounds and 2.5 steals per game for U18 Porsche Ludwigsburg, while leading the event in blocks (1.8 per game) and [[Performance Index Rating|index rating]] (26.7). He helped his team to fourth place and was named to the all-tournament team.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hein |first1=David |title=Camara named ANGT Valencia MVP |url=https://www.adidasngt.com/u18/news/latest/i/9d5mtqq4xfxwto36/camara-named-angt-valencia-mvp |publisher=Next Generation Tournament |accessdate=2 April 2020 |date=31 December 2018}}</ref> In 2019, Hukporti was honored as Rookie of the Year and All-Star Game MVP in the Nachwuchs Basketball Bundesliga (NBBL), the German U19 league.<ref name="nbbl">{{cite web |title=Awards der Nachwuchs Basketball Bundesliga |url=https://www.nbbl-basketball.de/events/awards-nbbl/ |publisher=NBBL |accessdate=2 April 2020 |language=German |archive-date=19 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220519223537/https://www.nbbl-basketball.de/events/awards-nbbl/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> He played for U18 Porsche Ludwigsburg at [[2019–20 Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament|ANGT]] [[2019–20 Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament#Munich, Germany|Munich]] in February 2020 but did not return to action after suffering a foot injury in his second game.<ref name="schmitz">{{cite web |last1=Schmitz |first1=Mike |title=Victor Wembanyama is one of the best long-term NBA prospects in the world |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/28686946/victor-wembanyama-one-best-long-term-nba-prospects-world |publisher=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=2 April 2020 |date=12 February 2020}}</ref> Hukporti was named NBBL MVP for the 2019–20 season after averaging 16.9 points and 9.4 rebounds per game for Porsche BBA Ludwigsburg.<ref>{{cite web |title=NBBL – Saisonawards 2019/20: Porsche BBA Ludwigsburg mit drei Auszeichnungen |url=https://www.nbbl-basketball.de/nbbl-saisonawards-2019-20-porsche-bba-ludwigsburg-mit-drei-auszeichnungen/ |publisher=NBBL |accessdate=28 June 2020 |language=German |date=6 June 2020}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Riesen Ludwigsburg (2018–2020)===
On 12 December 2018, Hukporti made his professional debut for [[Riesen Ludwigsburg]], scoring four points in one minute in an 88–76 loss to [[Bandırma B.İ.K.|Banvit]] at the [[Basketball Champions League]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Dec 12, 2018 – Teksut Bandirma 88 at MHP RIESEN Ludwigsburg 76 |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2018-12-12/Teksut-Bandirma-at-MHP-RIESEN-Ludwigsburg/326114 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |accessdate=2 April 2020 |date=12 December 2018}}</ref> On 13 January 2019, he debuted in the [[Basketball Bundesliga]] (BBL) versus [[medi Bayreuth]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Marcos Knight peitscht die MHP Riesen zum Sieg – Coach Patrick ist stolz |url=https://www.ludwigsburg24.com/marcos-knight-peitscht-die-mhp-riesen-zum-sieg-coach-patrick-ist-stolz/ |website=Ludwigsburg 24 |accessdate=2 April 2020 |language=German |date=14 January 2019}}</ref> At the [[2020 NBA All-Star Game#All-Star Weekend|NBA All-Star Weekend]] in [[Chicago]] in February 2020, Hukporti was named MVP of the [[Basketball Without Borders]] camp.<ref>{{cite web |title=Hukporti, Kessler named MVPs of BWB Global Camp |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/news/hukporti-kessler-named-mvps-of-bwb-global-camp |publisher=[[FIBA]] |accessdate=2 April 2020 |date=17 February 2020}}</ref> On 11 June 2020, he scored a career-high 10 points along with three rebounds and two blocks in a 103–74 win over [[Brose Bamberg]] in the preliminary round of the [[2019–20 Basketball Bundesliga#End of season tournament|2020 BBL Final Tournament]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Ludwigsburg routs Bamberg to close Day 3 |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/bbl/1069469/ludwigsburg-routs-bamberg-to-close-day-3/ |publisher=EuroHoops |accessdate=28 June 2020 |date=11 June 2020}}</ref> In the 2019–20 season, Hukporti averaged three points and 2.3 rebounds in 7.9 minutes per game.<ref name="realgm">{{cite web |title=Ariel Hukporti Player Profile |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Ariel-Hukporti/Summary/116911 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |accessdate=28 June 2020}}</ref>

===Nevėžis Kėdainiai (2020–2021)===
On 3 July 2020, Hukporti signed with [[BC Nevėžis|Nevėžis Kėdainiai]] of the [[Lietuvos krepšinio lyga|Lithuanian Basketball League]] (LKL).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/nevezis-adds-nba-prospect-abramo-canka-and-ariel-hukporti/|title=Nevezis adds NBA prospects Abramo Canka and Ariel Hukporti|last=|first=|date=3 July 2020|website=|publisher=Sportando|language=En|access-date=3 July 2020}}</ref>

===Melbourne United (2021–2024)===
On 28 July 2021, Hukporti signed as a [[NBL Next Stars Program|Next Star]] with [[Melbourne United]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL).<ref>{{Cite web|title=German NBA Prospect Ariel Hukporti Signs as NBL Next Star with Melbourne United|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/german-nba-prospect-ariel-hukporti-signs-as-nbl-next-star-with-melbourne-united|url-status=live|website=NBL.com.au|date=28 July 2021|access-date=28 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210727220309/https://nbl.com.au/news/german-nba-prospect-ariel-hukporti-signs-as-nbl-next-star-with-melbourne-united |archive-date=27 July 2021 }}</ref>

During the 2022 pre-season, Hukporti ruptured his achilles tendon and was ruled out for the entire [[2022–23 NBL season]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Hukporti Sidelined For NBL23|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/hukporti-sidelined-for-nbl23|website=NBL.com.au|date=22 September 2022|access-date=22 September 2022}}</ref>

On 31 March 2023, Hukporti recommitted to United for the [[2023–24 NBL season]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ariel Hukporti set to return to the court for NBL24|url=https://www.melbourneutd.com.au/news/ariel-hukporti-set-to-return-to-the-court-for-nbl24|website=melbourneutd.com.au|date=31 March 2023|access-date=31 March 2023}}</ref>

===Return to Riesen Ludwigsburg (2024)===
On 1 April 2024, Hukporti signed with [[Riesen Ludwigsburg]] for the rest of the [[2023–24 Basketball Bundesliga]] season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Willkommen daheim, Ariel!|url=https://mhp-riesen-ludwigsburg.de/news/willkommen-daheim-ariel/|website=MHP-Riesen-Ludwigsburg.de|date=1 April 2024|access-date=2 April 2024|language=de}}</ref>

===New York Knicks (2024–2026)===
On 27 June 2024, Hukporti was selected with the 58th overall pick by the [[Dallas Mavericks]] in the [[2024 NBA draft]], which was the draft's final pick.<ref>{{cite web|first=Geoff|last=Magliocchetti|title=Knicks Close Draft With Ariel Hukporti|url=https://mmsport.minutemediabeta.com/allknicks/draft-coverage/new-york-knicks-close-draft-with-ariel-hukporti|website=Sports Illustrated|date=27 June 2024|access-date=29 June 2024}}</ref> On the same day, his draft rights were traded to the [[New York Knicks]] in exchange for the rights of [[Melvin Ajinça]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Dwain|last=Price|title=Mavs make draft-day trade for forward Melvin Ajinca|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavstradeforajinca/|website=Mavs.com|date=27 June 2024|access-date=28 June 2024}}</ref> On 8 July 2024, he signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Knicks.<ref>{{cite web|title=New York Knicks Sign Ariel Hukporti to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/news/new-york-knicks-sign-ariel-hukporti-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=8 July 2024|access-date=17 July 2024}}</ref>

Hukporti made his NBA debut on 22 October 2024, in a 132–109 loss to the [[Boston Celtics]]<ref>{{cite web|title=New York Knicks at Boston Celtics Box Score, October 22, 2024|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202410220BOS.html|website=BasketballRef|date=22 October 2024|access-date=26 October 2024}}</ref> and on 4 November, he signed a standard contract with the Knicks.<ref>{{cite tweet|author=NY_KnicksPR|title=.@nyknicks Sign Ariel Hukporti|number=1853890063421038988|user=NY_KnicksPR|date=5 November 2024|access-date=5 November 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Sources: Knicks, Hukporti agree on two-year deal|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/42189139/knicks-ariel-hukporti-agree-standard-2-year-deal|website=ESPN.com|date=4 November 2024|access-date=4 November 2024}}</ref> Throughout his rookie season, he was [[NBA G League#Standard assignment|assigned]] several times to the [[Westchester Knicks]].<ref>{{cite web|title=2024-2025 Westchester Knicks Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Westchester-Knicks/40/Transaction_History/2025|website=RealGM.com|access-date=18 December 2024}}</ref> Hukporti made his first career start on 26 February 2025 against the [[2024–25 Philadelphia 76ers season|Philadelphia 76ers]], recording 8 points, 2 rebounds, and 1 block. However, Hukporti suffered a [[meniscus tear|torn meniscus]] in the game, and was ruled out for 4-6 weeks.<ref>{{cite web |last=Charania |first=Shams |author-link=Shams Charania |date=2025-02-27 |title=Sources: Knicks' Hukporti suffers torn meniscus |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/44041221/sources-knicks-ariel-hukporti-4-6-weeks-torn-meniscus |access-date=2025-12-06 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

In Game 4 of the [[2026 NBA Finals]], a 29-point comeback win against the [[San Antonio Spurs]], Hukporti played in the first quarter after [[Karl-Anthony Towns]] got into foul trouble and had a block on a [[Dylan Harper]] layup in a game the Knicks won by one point. In Game 5 of the Finals, Hukporti helped the Knicks achieve a 94–90 win and close out the NBA Finals against the Spurs, 4–1, securing the Knicks' first NBA championship in 53 years.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/new-york-knicks/knicks-news-first-championship-53-years-nba-finals-spurs|title=Knicks win first championship in 53 years after NBA Finals Game 5 triumph vs. Spurs|website=ClutchPoints|last=Siegel|first=Brett|date=June 13, 2026|access-date=June 13, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/news/live-updates-2026-nba-finals-game-5-knicks-seek-first-title-since-1973|title=Recap: The Knicks win the 2026 NBA championship|website=NBA.com|last=Lambert|first=Ben|date=June 13, 2026|access-date=June 13, 2026}}</ref>

=== Philadelphia 76ers (2026–present) ===
On 6 July 2026, Hukporti signed a one-year, $3.4 million contract with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=PHILADELPHIA 76ERS SIGN ARIEL HUKPORTI |url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/philadelphia-76erssign-ariel-hukporti |access-date=July 6, 2026 |publisher=[[Philadelphia 76ers]]}}</ref>

==National team career==
Hukporti represented [[Germany national under-17 basketball team|Germany]] at the [[2017 FIBA U16 European Championship]] in [[Podgorica]]. He averaged 5.4 points, 8.9 rebounds and 1.4 blocks for the 13th-place team.<ref name="gershon">{{cite web |last1=Gershon |first1=Josh |title=FIBA u16 A: Ariel Hukporti putting name on map with Germany |url=https://www.scout.com/Article/FIBA-u16-A-2019-center-Ariel-Hukporti-putting-name-on-map-with-Germany-106045400/ |publisher=[[Scout.com]] |accessdate=2 April 2020 |date=12 August 2017}}</ref> In April 2018, he won a gold medal with Germany at the [[Albert Schweitzer Tournament]].<ref name=big/> Later that year, at the [[2018 FIBA U16 European Championship|FIBA U16 European Championship]] in [[Novi Sad]], Hukporti averaged 9.6 points and 5.9 rebounds, leading his team to ninth place.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ariel Hukporti (GER)'s profile – FIBA U16 European Championship 2018 |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u16/2018/player/Ariel-Hukporti |publisher=[[FIBA]] |accessdate=2 April 2020}}</ref> He averaged 10.1 points, 6.4 rebounds and 1.6 blocks at the [[2019 FIBA U18 European Championship]] in [[Volos]] as his team finished in 11th place.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hein |first1=David |title=ANGT Munich: Players to Watch |url=https://www.adidasngt.com/u18/news/latest/i/abo7ada9s7d5slrp/angt-munich-players-to-watch |publisher=Next Generation Tournament |accessdate=2 April 2020 |date=15 January 2020}}</ref>
